1.title: Azure App Service
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Azure App Service. It covers the exam area Deploy and manage Azure compute resources. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Provision an App Service plan. Configure scaling for an App Service plan. Create an App Service. Configure certificates and T L S for an App Service. Map an existing custom D N S name to an App Service. Configure backup for an App Service. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (twenty-twenty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: App Service and the plan
1.text: App Service and the plan. Azure App Service is a managed platform for web apps, A P Is and mobile back ends in.N E T, Java, Node.js, Python, P H P and containers. Azure manages the O S, patching and load balancing. The App Service plan is the compute the apps run on: it sets the region, operating system, size and features. Several apps can share one plan (they share its C P U and memory).

1.title: App Service and the plan, continued
1.text: App Service and the plan. Free or Shared. Dev and test, shared compute, no custom T L S, no scale-out. Basic. Dedicated compute, custom domains and T L S, manual scale (up to three). Standard. Autoscale, deployment slots, backups. Premium (v three). More slots and instances, faster hardware, zone redundancy. Isolated. Dedicated environment in your V net (App Service Environment). Exam tip: Deployment slots, autoscale and scheduled backups need Standard or higher.

1.title: Scaling
1.text: Scaling. The figure shows this: Scale up (bigger instance) compared with scale out (more instances).

1.title: Scaling, continued
1.text: Scaling. Scale up (vertical). Change to a bigger plan or tier (more C P U, memory, features). Scale out (horizontal). Add instances of the app. Manual. You set the instance count. Autoscale. Rules (C P U, memory, H T T P queue) or a schedule change the count within min and max limits (Standard and above).

1.title: Certificates, TLS and custom domains
1.text: Certificates, T L S and custom domains. Custom domain. Needs Basic or higher; verify ownership with a T X T record ( asuid ) and add a C N A M E (subdomain) or A (root) record. Certificates. App Service Managed Certificate (free, auto-renews), certificate from Key Vault, or upload your own. T L S binding. Bind the certificate to the custom domain (S N I S S L). H T T P S Only. Redirects H T T P to H T T P S. Minimum T L S version. Set (for example one point two) to reject older protocols.

1.title: Certificates, TLS and custom domains, continued
1.text: Certificates, T L S and custom domains. The figure shows this: Mapping a custom domain: D N S records, domain verification and a T L S binding.

1.title: Backup
1.text: Backup. Tier. Standard or higher. What. App files, configuration and connected databases. Where. A storage account container. Schedule. Automatic backups are on by default in newer tiers; custom backups let you set the schedule and retention. Restore. To the same app, a new app, or a slot.

1.title: Networking
1.text: Networking. V net integration. Direction: Outbound. Purpose: Let the app reach resources in a V net (databases, V Ms). Private endpoint. Direction: Inbound. Purpose: Give the app a private I P so clients reach it privately. Access restrictions. Direction: Inbound. Purpose: Allow or deny by I P, subnet or service tag. Hybrid connections. Direction: Outbound. Purpose: Reach an on-premises T C P endpoint without opening inbound ports.

1.title: Deployment slots
1.text: Deployment slots. A deployment slot is a live app with its own host name (for example myapp staging ) in the same plan. Swap. Exchange the staging slot with production; the slot is warmed up first, so no downtime, and you can swap back. Slot settings. Mark app settings or connection strings as slot settings so they stay with the slot during a swap. Traffic routing. Send a percentage of production traffic to a slot for testing in production. Tier. Standard or higher. Exam tip: "Deploy a new version and switch with no downtime and an easy rollback" equals deployment slot swap.

1.title: Deployment slots, continued
1.text: Deployment slots. Exam tip: Slot swaps, autoscale and backups need Standard or higher; custom domains need Basic or higher.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team wants to deploy a new version of a web app and switch to it with no downtime and an easy rollback. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A deployment slot with a swap. Slot swaps warm up the new version and can be swapped back.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An app must add instances automatically when C P U is high. What is the minimum tier that supports autoscale? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Standard. Autoscale requires Standard or higher.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which D N S record helps verify ownership of a custom domain for App Service? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A T X T record. A T X T record with the asuid value verifies ownership.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A web app must connect to a database in a virtual network. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: V net integration. V net integration provides outbound access to V net resources.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Clients should reach an App Service only through a private I P address. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A private endpoint. A private endpoint makes inbound access private.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. An administrator wants an app setting to stay with the staging slot during a swap. What should be done? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Mark it as a slot setting. Slot settings are sticky to the slot.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does an App Service plan define? Answer: The region, operating system, size and features of the compute. Question two. Which tiers support deployment slots? Answer: Standard and higher. Question three. What is the difference between scale up and scale out? Answer: Scale up uses a bigger plan; scale out adds instances.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does H T T P S Only do? Answer: Redirects H T T P requests to H T T P S. Question five. Is V net integration inbound or outbound? Answer: Outbound. Question six. What is the free option for a certificate? Answer: An App Service Managed Certificate.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Plan: region, O S, size; apps share it; Standard plus for slots, autoscale, backup. Scaling: scale up (bigger) versus scale out (more); autoscale rules or schedule. T L S and D N S: Basic plus for custom domains; T X T verification; managed certificate; H T T P S Only. Networking: V net integration (out), private endpoint (in), access restrictions. Slots: swap, slot settings, traffic routing, no downtime. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
